fields.statement: The conduct-handback, conduct-roles and workflows guide topics, docs/primitives.md, docs/runs-and-daemon.md, docs/bring-your-own-agent.md and docs/examples/byo/conductor.toml describe the ship steps' own rebase: conduct-handback has routes for pr-green and rebase as conduct-handback-routes-ship-rebase decides and none for merge, never tells the conductor to run rhiza ship rebase, conduct-roles gives conflict-fix for a code conflict the ship steps leave in progress, workflows lists ship-change's 12 steps, runs-and-daemon.md's ship-change entry lists the 12 steps (with pr-green and rebase) and says a failed merge goes to rebase instead of every red up to the merge handing back, primitives.md's Wait and Merge sections show wait-ci without --no-rebase and the pr-green, merge and rebase steps, and the byo conductor example copies the built-in's steps after conduct (wait-ci on rhiza ship check --settled, pr-green, merge, rebase) so bring-your-own-agent.md's "Everything after conduct is the built-in's" holds, its hand-back paragraph naming pr-green and rebase instead of a failed merge.

set.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow -run TestBuiltinShipChange shows the steps and routes ship-steps-rebase-clean's acceptance gives, the conduct step declaring exactly the checks plan, code and qa, the gate step of kind gate with its four commands, the hand-back cap at 3 and no leaves or checks step; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestBuildCheck shows build-check failing on a leaf with no Evidence; rhiza workflow describe ship-change lists those steps.
set.statement: The builtin ship-change is the conductor default: conduct (the conduct skill, its step declaring the review checks plan, code and qa), gate (a step of the gate step kind running rhiza run build-check, rhiza run review-check, rhiza check and rhiza ship gate; the pre-push check runs inside the push step's rhiza ship open-pr and inside rhiza ship rebase), signoff, push and open the PR, wait for CI at that head (rhiza ship check --settled, which merges main on a conflicting PR), pr-green (rhiza ship check), merge the tested head (rhiza ship merge), rebase (rhiza ship rebase, back to the CI wait), main's CI (one step), close-out, ship (rhiza ship command) and deploy-check (rhiza ship deploy), as ship-steps-rebase-clean gives them; every red result before the merge (conduct, gate, signoff, push, wait-ci and pr-green) hands back to conduct, at most three times; every merge fail (main moved, or a gh, fetch or git error) goes to the rebase step, which hands back only on a code conflict or a local gate or pre-push check failing on the merged head. The steps after the merge (main's CI, close-out, ship and deploy-check) have no on.fail route and no hand-back: nothing on the branch can fix a merged change set. A draft or a merge GitHub refused stops the run (rhiza ship merge's stop exit).

set.acceptance: In this repo, rhiza workflow describe ship-change resolves to the builtin; rhiza workflow describe ship-rhiza shows the [env], the go-cleanup cleanup running sh .rhiza/workflows/go-cleanup.sh, the builtin's 12 steps and every hand-back route as handback:ship-change/conduct; rhiza workflow describe bugfix still shows the go-cleanup cleanup and its hand-back routes as handback:ship-change/conduct; rhiza workflow check passes with no new warning beyond the autonomous ones AGENTS.md expects; rhiza check accepts .rhiza/dispatch.toml naming ship-rhiza for [ready] feature and bugfix for bug; go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow -run TestShipFixPromptsOneLine passes with .rhiza/workflows/ship-change.toml gone, its repo-file loop reading ship-rhiza and docs; make self-check passes. Touches .rhiza/workflows/ship-change.toml (removed), .rhiza/workflows/ship-rhiza.toml, .rhiza/dispatch.toml, .rhiza/workflows/bugfix.toml and internal/workflow/workflow_test.go (only TestShipFixPromptsOneLine's repo-file loop).

set.statement: (1) The new builtin ship-change keeps ship (rhiza ship command) and deploy-check (rhiza ship deploy) after close-out, unchanged: conduct, gate, signoff, push/PR, CI, pr-green, merge, rebase, main CI, close-out, ship, deploy is exactly 12 steps (10 when first decided; ship-steps-rebase-clean-merge adds pr-green and rebase). (2) A red main CI after the merge stops the run, as classic does: main-green has no on.fail route and no hand-back, and its output says main is red after the merge of this change set; the hand-back rule covers every red before the merge. (3) Rhiza's shadow .rhiza/workflows/ship-change.toml is removed; its [env] (GOTMPDIR, SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA, SHIP_HEAD_BUILD) moves to a thin repo workflow .rhiza/workflows/ship-rhiza.toml that includes the builtin ship-change (like bugfix.toml does), and .rhiza/dispatch.toml sets [ready] feature = "ship-rhiza"; bugfix.toml keeps its own [env]. The builtin has no head-build steps: the ship commands that land or render run SHIP_HEAD_BUILD themselves before doing so when it is set, as ship rebase already does. (4) The classic tests stay and are pointed at ship-change-classic (by name, or with the workflow pinned in the script), since classic stays available and pinnable; only the tests of the default itself (bugfix-workflow-autonomous, daemon-root-ship-workflow, the daemon pick tests that assert the default's steps) move to the new builtin, and the new builtin gets its own tests (TestBuiltinShipChange, ship-change-one-ci). No classic test is deleted.
